# arduino-cli

**Command-line toolchain for compiling and uploading Arduino-framework firmware**

- **Version recorded:** 1.5.1
- **Categories:** `hardware`, `workstation`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/arduino/arduino-cli>

## What it does

Compiles and uploads Arduino-framework sketches from the command line, manages board support packages and libraries, and lists attached boards with the ports and cores they need.

## Why you would want it

Several devices in this catalog run Arduino-framework firmware, and building it from a terminal is reproducible in a way the graphical IDE is not. It is also the fastest way to identify which core a connected board wants.

## Before it will work

Membership of the `dialout` group and a board support package for whatever you are targeting, which it downloads on first use. On Debian 13 and Parrot the package is not available at all.

## How it installs

- apt: `arduino-cli` — *on kali*
  - Kali only. Absent from Debian 13 and Parrot. Upstream ships prebuilt binaries, which would need the binary backend plus a pinned checksum; that is deliberately not claimed here until it is tested.

## Known problems

Not packaged for Debian 13 or Parrot — Kali only. Board support packages are fetched from the network on first use, which is worth doing before taking a machine into the field. ModemManager grabbing a newly attached board for twenty seconds makes upload fail in a way that looks like a wiring problem.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
